Kento Alpha 0.9.31, build 2831

Fixes

  • The Viewer is drawn the size of its panel when Kento starts. It could be pinned small in the panel's top left, with an old picture showing around it, until another layout was chosen.
  • Kento no longer crashes when you go through the Mac menu bar's submenus (Edit's, for one): a submenu is built whole as its menu opens.
  • The Viewer no longer says a frame is missing past a Read's range when the Read holds its last frame there.
  • Window > Workspaces > Paint opens; it failed to load.
  • Right-clicking a node in the Node Graph no longer fails on a node whose control is linked straight to another node's.
  • A comp with a BoxOut that isn't wired yet saves, and autosaves. Every save of it failed.
  • A TVIscale2 with nothing wired no longer fills the log with errors.
  • A panel button that needs something first, like Axis's Read file with no file chosen, says so in a tip by the button. Before, nothing happened.
  • The Viewer's tabs are the same size as the other panels' tabs.

New

  • Edit > Node > Swap A and B (⇧X) swaps the selected nodes' first two inputs, a Merge's A and B. The mask stays where it is.
  • The Playback pop-up has a Playback cache switch, to play every frame live, and Clear the cache.
  • Colorspace has every one of Nuke's spaces: 2.40, 2.60, BT1886, PLogLin, SLog, SLog1, SLog2, CLog, HybridLogGamma, Protune, st2084, Blackmagic Film Generation 5 and ARRILogC4 are added, checked against NukeX. They stopped the render before.
  • Kento's remote control can file a problem report or a suggestion, open the report window filled in, and open My reports.

Nuke scripts

  • A Roto or RotoPaint that uses something Kento doesn't draw as Nuke does yet (a clip to its input's box, strokes' motion blur, or a kind of stroke Kento doesn't draw) is named when the script comes in, and its node has an amber dot that says what. Pre-comp such a node in Nuke and read the render in its place.
  • A Write left at its default color space takes the LUT for its data type, as Nuke does: an 8-bit TIFF Write took the 16-bit one.
  • A Dilate keeps up when only the picture above it changes size (a Crop moved); it could keep the earlier size and cut the picture off.
  • A Read's frame field works in its expression mode, as in Nuke: a number holds that frame, and words like frame-1000 or frame/2 pick the file's frame at each frame. It was ignored.
  • Expression and MergeExpression take min and max of more than two values, as Nuke does: min(r,g,b) stopped the node. Every Expression in the studio's comps now reads.

Kento Alpha 0.9.30, build 2807

Report a problem

  • Reports are filed again: 0.9.29 couldn't reach the studio bug tracker, and kept every report to send later. A report kept that way is filed soon after 0.9.30 starts.
  • Reports no longer land on the Desktop. Kento writes them to its own folder and removes a report's .zip once the tracker has it: the tracker keeps the files, and removes them a few weeks after the report is resolved. A report that stays on this Mac is shown in Finder.
  • Grab a panel works: a click on a panel failed, and a panel's picture came out black.
  • Record voice says when macOS has refused Kento the microphone, and where to allow it (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone), where it recorded nothing.
  • My reports says when the tracker has removed a report's files.

Fixes

  • Picking a color from the Viewer shows an eyedropper pointer, its tip where the pick lands.
  • Optimize shows what it measured; it stayed at "Measuring frame 1".

Kento Alpha 0.9.29, build 2800

Report a problem

  • Help > My reports shows each filed report's conversation with the pipeline team: Your turn when they've written and wait on you, New reply for a message you haven't read. The speech button shows the conversation under the report, and Send answer replies under the report's name.
  • When the pipeline team answers one of your reports, a card in the window's corner says so, even with My reports closed.
  • Reports are filed to the studio bug tracker by its name, tools.vpn.byautonomy.com.

Matching Nuke

  • A Reformat that scales samples the picture exactly as Nuke does; a scale of 1.53 was about 1% off.
  • A plate reduced with Reformat keeps its edge's brightness: its outer column and row came out up to 9% dark.
  • Switch past its last input shows the last input, and an empty input in the middle shows nothing, as in Nuke.
  • Merge's bbox A takes in every A input.
  • A TIFF or DPX left at colorspace default takes Root's LUT for its bit depth, as Nuke does.
  • Roto: a shape's hard side, where its feather points sit on it, is anti-aliased as Nuke draws it, and curved feather bands are closer to Nuke's.
